cursor.note: standing() now asks ONE question — did the newest entry come whole through persist_validation — and it asks it by READING inspect_trail's lane record rather than walking the trail a second time. The Merkle property is what makes that sufficient: a link hashes the trail beneath it, so tampering with any older entry necessarily breaks the newest link. The seven unlinked entries from 2026-08-07/08 are left exactly where they are — history, not damage to repair. And the reason they happened is closed at the source: run_proof takes a REQUIRED, no-default sink and `cairn test --seal` can land a verdict, so the affordance a builder had to route around the physics to get now exists. The half that matters more is that a non-sealing run SAYS it sealed nothing — that silence is how the gap stayed invisible for eight days while it was being worked around.

window.standing: PROVED — THE VALIDATION TRAIL'S DOOR IS NOW THE ONLY PATH (ticket validation-store-door-is-the-only-path, P1, drained from the live trouble). The trail was a record of truth declared APPEND-ONLY by its door and stored as a plain 0644 JSON file: a hand-write destroyed a proof's whole seal history silently and permanently, and looked exactly like a fresh seal (Law 7's worst direction). Closed in three layers that answer three different failure modes — the MODE BIT (0444) stops the accident at the open(); the CHAIN (a door-minted trail_link per record, sha256 over the trail beneath it plus the record itself) makes the deliberate loud, and standing() refuses a broken trail rather than reading a verdict out of it, so harbor_master clears nothing on it; the CORPUS SCAN refuses a second writer at BUILD time rather than at runtime. THE PROOF KILLED THE FIRST DESIGN: a tolerated unlinked prefix ("prehistory") is indistinguishable from a total overwrite, which is the exact destroy-the-history shape the trouble named — a tolerance is a forger's costume whenever the forger can produce the thing tolerated. So the 73 legacy trails were ADOPTED instead: 220 entries linked, all verify, idempotent, and adoption REFUSES to re-link a tampered trail. quorum.record_verdict now returns what LANDED, not what it built (the assembled dict was a second, unlinked copy — the rival-source-of-truth defect MethodRegistry already was). NAMED, NOT GLOSSED: the bytes stay writable to the same uid, nothing here un-destroys a trail, and git carries only the exec bit so a fresh clone lands 0644 until the door next appends — the chain is the half that survives a clone. 9/9 teeth (6 new), quorum 9/9, corpus 86 · 85 green · 1 red over four consecutive runs.

The false remedy 'recover the trail from git' is gone — measured, git holds no linked version — replaced by the true one. run_proof gained a REQUIRED no-default sink ('validations' | 'none') that persists through persist_validation and mints nothing; every call site in the corpus names it, and constrain_floor names 'none' so a chart stage cannot seal. `cairn test --seal` grew, and every run now says out loud whether it sealed. The two stale trails were re-run through --seal: 20->21 and 2->3 entries, every pre-existing entry byte-identical by sha256, both now proven, nothing edited or adopted. 5 new teeth (16 in test_validation_store, 8 in test_tester, both rosters floored); 3 observed FAILING against pre-change code loaded via `git show HEAD` — the stronger instrument, no stash, working tree untouched. The corpus census tooth reads all 90 real trails and is required to red on a known-bad fixture corpus AND on an empty glob. Proved twice. Whole corpus: 111 proofs, 109 green, 2 red — both RED AT HEAD in a clean worktree, both raised through the trouble door rather than passed over.
